body.statement: For any fixed nonempty finite \(\mathfrak G\), nonempty compact boxes, exponent array, and nonempty open \(\mathcal O\subset(0,1)^p\), there are a finite rational \(\mathcal T\subset\mathcal O\), a rational \(r_{\mathrm{id}}>0\), and a valid finite rational chart-projection cover \(\mathscr C\) such that \(\Gamma_{\mathcal T}>0\), \(\kappa_{\mathcal T}>0\), \(\Lambda_{\mathcal T}(r_{\mathrm{id}})>0\), and \(\mu_{\mathcal T}(r_{\mathrm{id}};\mathscr C)>0\). Here \(\Gamma_{\mathcal T}=+\infty\) when \(|\mathfrak G|=1\), and \(\Lambda_{\mathcal T}=+\infty\) when its remote pair set is empty. Consequently each within-graph moment map is globally injective; this uses local chart strong monotonicity and remote separation, not the Jacobian margin alone.
body.justification: This establishes existence of a finite transform design with distinct global and local certificates.
body.gap: Bodik--Chavez-Demoulin supplies neither a finite PGF grid nor quantitative global-injectivity and Jacobian margins over compact boxes.
body.consumer: It supplies the consistency check that the reusable certificate is searching for a nonvacuous finite-input object.
